title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on group points

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed NIST P-256 generator P, the parallel Pollard rho algorithm of proof.md (R=2048 adding walks on the affine x high-bit partition, look-ahead, distinguished points of 32 trailing zero x-bits, w=2^40 walks, k=46*2^123 point budget, batched affine steps) recovers x with success probability at least 0.64 under the disclosed random-mapping idealization M1 stated there, using at most 2^129.687061 total target-group-operation equivalents including preprocessing, all trials and failures, randomness, DP table work, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^103.108525 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27.288456 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged precomputation, oracle or amortization over future targets.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical plain R-adding walk with look-ahead and distinguished points end-to-end on a small prime-order Weierstrass curve (p=1999, r=2089), measuring steps-to-solve against the sqrt(pi r/2) idealization and counting unsolvable relations. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
